assessment: The engine wins the board and then asks how to close. Four bench cards make the ten because each completes a line whose other pieces are already sleeved: Gravecrawler, Reassembling Skeleton, Exquisite Blood, Grave Pact. Six pool cards beat the bench tail — Nim Deathmantle, Warren Soultrader, Ayara, Black Sun's Zenith and Gray Merchant of Asphodel over Cabal Coffers, Crypt Ghast, Sheoldred and Urborg, and Plumb the Forbidden over Imp's Mischief. Ownership is the uncomfortable part: nine of the ten cards behind the Considering: marker appear in none of the pilot's seven decklist files, and only Black Sun's Zenith and Plumb the Forbidden below are already in the box.

The Avatar carries stack 005 and the Exquisite Blood line; Ophiomancer carries neither, so Ophiomancer is the half to move.

bench_verdicts.why: The one bench card the pilot already owns, and the one that does least: mana_analysis counts 35 of the deck's 36 lands already producing black, so Urborg's marginal contribution is making Ancient Tomb tap for {B}. It earns a slot the day Cabal Coffers or Crypt Ghast is sleeved.

Twenty-two Swamps make it a genuine engine, but the goldfish says the shortage is death-triggered mana at 53.0%, not total mana — mean available mana is 5.2 by turn 6 against a curve that stops at 6. Warren Soultrader took the slot because it fixes the number that is actually low.
Same axis as Cabal Coffers, one turn later and on a body that dies to everything. The provisional role budget already has the deck over on ramp at 11 against 10.
The same effect as Grave Pact one mana higher, and flash is a real difference — but Grave Pact is on the ten, so this is duplicated function, and the corpus is blunt about which to cut first.

Mono-black's only answer to a counterspell, and the protection budget is short by one. It loses to Plumb the Forbidden, which answers the card that actually ends this deck — a sweeper — and draws a handful doing it.

Seven mana on a list whose curve stops at six, in a seat with 5.8 mean available mana on turn 7. Reanimation plus an upkeep edict is exactly what the deck wants; the cost is a turn it usually does not get.

gaps: Ownership is the finding, not a footnote. Nine of the ten cards behind the Considering: marker appear in none of the pilot's seven decklist files — Reassembling Skeleton and Gravecrawler among them — so the bench is a shopping list rather than a box. Only Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth is owned (Hapatra.txt). Of the ten above, Black Sun's Zenith (Hapatra.txt) and Plumb the Forbidden (Black.txt) are in the box; the other eight are purchases.

Not one line on this list is verified. Six stacks pass — 001 through 006 — and they cover the Blowfly Infestation loop, the four drains and the entering-counter rules question; none of them touches a card named above. The two highest-value /resolve-stack targets are Exquisite Blood + South Wind Avatar (does the loop terminate, and does it close a four-player table) and Nim Deathmantle + Ashnod's Altar + Grave Titan (does the Titan's own tokens pay the {4}).

The combo DB's card lists are not always complete, and this deck is where that shows. It records Gravecrawler + Phyrexian Altar as a two-card infinite, but the oracle text needs a second Zombie on the battlefield before the recast is legal — the record is missing a piece the deck happens to have six of. Same class of gap: it records Thran Vigil + Viscera Seer as a two-card infinite, but Thran Vigil only loops with a persist creature and the 99 holds none, so that hit is not a pick.

An obsolescence hit refuted by reading the card: obsolescence_index.json lists Postmortem Professor, Tunnel Rats, Purple Pentapus and Cantor of the Refrain as strictly better than Reassembling Skeleton on power and toughness. Only Postmortem Professor is in the box (Black.txt), and its recursion exiles an instant or sorcery from the graveyard each time — a finite resource, so it cannot loop, which is the only job the Skeleton is on this list for.

Two more index hits that should not be acted on. Boggart Mischief (Auntie Ool.txt) is listed as an upgrade over Bastion of Remembrance, but its drain triggers only on Goblin deaths and the 99 holds one Goblin, while Bastion reads every creature the pilot controls. Last Gasp (Black.txt, Auntie Ool.txt) is listed as an upgrade over Dismember on 'Lower CMC', but Dismember's Phyrexian pips cast it for {1} and 4 life and kill a larger body — and neither card places -1/-1 counters, so neither feeds Nest of Scarabs.

How many Insects one Black Sun's Zenith makes depends on whether Nest of Scarabs triggers once per creature or once per counter-placing event. That is a triggered-ability question, not a data one, and no figure should be printed until /resolve-stack settles it.

Ad Nauseam is in the box (Hapatra.txt) and the computed floor tolerates it — 4 before, 4 after. It is off the ten anyway: this list already pays life to Yawgmoth, Necropotence, Toxic Deluge, Bitterblossom, Black Market Connections, Ancient Tomb and City of Brass, and nothing measured here says how much life is spare.

card_roles.json has no entry for Plumb the Forbidden, so its role chip is blank. Absence of a role is not absence of the function — the taxonomy simply has no pattern for a scaling instant-speed sacrifice draw spell.
